findings.title: Total-price law has no Swiss PBV legal floor, only a UX-conversion framing
findings.principle: Every price shown to a Swiss consumer at the moment a booking becomes a purchase offer (the first screen where a service price appears, not just at Bezahlen) must be the actual total price payable in CHF, including VAT and any non-optional surcharge, per Preisbekanntgabeverordnung (PBV) Art. 10 and SECO's own clarification that hidden, link-only, or checkout-only price components do not satisfy disclosure. This is a legal floor, independent of and stricter in enforcement risk than the conversion-motivated 'relative label only if small and next to the absolute price' allowance in PSYCHOLOGY.md law 5, and the file must say so explicitly rather than reading as a pure A/B-testable optimization.
findings.why: PSYCHOLOGY.md law 5 was derived entirely from Baymard abandonment research, a UX metric, not from Swiss law. If a future add-on or surcharge feature leans on the 'relative label ... only when genuinely small' allowance without independently satisfying PBV's own total-price-at-the-purchase-offer-moment test, Solen risks a SECO or Lauterkeitskommission enforcement action regardless of any conversion outcome. A legal floor and a UX best practice can diverge, and only one carries a fine or injunction risk; right now they are written as if they are the same rule.
findings.local_evidence: PSYCHOLOGY.md line 28 (law 5): 'Add-on prices may use a relative label ("2.9% des Preises") ONLY directly next to the visible absolute price, only when genuinely small and fair.' No PBV, SECO, or Preisbekanntgabeverordnung citation anywhere in the file. bookings.platform_fee (lib/types.ts:244, app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:155) is currently a salon-side commission taken via Stripe application_fee, not a customer-facing line item, but the code path and the relative-label allowance both exist, and nothing stops a future customer-facing surcharge from leaning on the allowance without a PBV check.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i "PBV|Preisbekanntgabe|price indication ordinance" _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md _backend-system -> zero hits. grep -rn -i "VAT|MwSt" across the same paths -> zero hits tied to consumer price display. WebSearch on SECO/e-commerce-guide.admin.ch confirmed PBV requires the actual price payable be disclosed 'at the time and place of the purchase offer, not only shortly before contract conclusion' and that 'hidden, only linked, or checkout-only price components do not meet these requirements.'
findings.existing_coverage: partial: PSYCHOLOGY.md law 5 and hard line 3 already require total-price-from-step-one as a conversion law, and in spirit it is stricter than PBV's minimum. The gap is that the file never names PBV as a separate, non-negotiable legal floor, so the relative-label carve-out reads as tunable UX policy rather than something bounded by law.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md (new hard line cross-referencing law 5) and _rules/ (a dedicated compliance note, since PBV is legal, not taste)
findings.enforcement: checklist: no regex can verify 'is this the actual total, in CHF, at the purchase-offer moment' from source alone; add a named line to the pre-ship checklist for any new surcharge/fee feature, reviewed against the PBV text rather than only A/B tested

findings.title: A user's stored notification-consent preference has no structural guarantee any sender actually reads it
findings.principle: Every user-facing consent or preference toggle (notification category switches, marketing opt-in, a future personalization opt-out) must have at least one automated check proving a real send-path reads that exact column before the toggle ships, using the same discriminate-the-behavior standard CLAUDE.md already requires for search filters ('a filter must DISCRIMINATE... not just render or return 200'). A consent flag that renders and saves but is never read by the code that actually sends is not a UX-bug-tier issue; it is a false consent claim to the user, and should be treated with the same severity as a security silent no-op, not a cosmetic defect.
findings.why: CLAUDE.md's existing silent-no-op doctrine is written entirely around search and filter correctness (PostgREST swallowing a bad column, isOpenNow reading the wrong day-keys); it never names CONSENT flags as a distinct case, even though a consent flag that silently does nothing is a materially worse failure than a silent filter: the user is told 'you turned this off' while an entirely separate code path with no such check keeps contacting them. The audit already caught this happening twice, independently, in the same codebase, on the same date, which is exactly the pattern that should generalize into a named rule rather than stay two isolated bug tickets.
findings.local_evidence: PSYCH_AUDIT_2026-07-07.md line 533: SettingsForm's notification_sms toggle has zero read sites anywhere outside its own save round-trip; the one real SMS sender (app/api/cron/sms-reminders/route.ts) gates on a different, salon-level column entirely and never checks the user's own preference. PSYCH_AUDIT_2026-07-07.md line 551: app/api/cron/barber-smart-reminders/route.ts:108-118 sends SMS with no notification_preferences check at all, while its sibling crons (rebooking-nudge/route.ts:60-65, confirmed live in this session; nail-infill-reminders/route.ts:59-63) do check the equivalent flag, an inconsistency the same audit pass caught in two different crons on the same day.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i "consent.*no-op|preference.*discriminat|opt-out.*test|notification.*silent" CLAUDE.md _rules -> zero hits; CLAUDE.md's Silent no-ops section names only search filters, computed filters, and opening_hours day-keys as examples, never a consent or preference toggle.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the general silent-no-op doctrine and its 'prove behavior, not existence' test already exist in CLAUDE.md and would catch exactly this bug class if applied; the delta is that consent and preference flags are never named as a discriminate-worthy category, so nobody ran the existing test against them until one 2026-07-07 audit did it by hand.
findings.where_it_should_live: CLAUDE.md Silent no-ops section (add consent/notification-preference flags as a named example category) and _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md enforcement section
findings.enforcement: gate: extend the existing exists-check tooling, or add a lightweight grep-based CI check flagging any notification_preferences.* or profiles.notification_* column with zero non-write read sites under app/api/cron/*

findings.title: The entire psychology/ethics law layer scopes to customer surfaces only; the salon (B2B) dashboard has zero coverage
findings.principle: Every hard ethics line in PSYCHOLOGY.md (no fabricated numbers, no pre-checked paid add-ons, no dark-pattern countdowns, no forced continuity) must bind the salon/business dashboard exactly as it binds customer-facing screens, because the dashboard is where Solen could nudge a salon owner, a B2B customer with real money at stake via Stripe Connect payouts and commission, using the same manipulative patterns the customer-facing rules already ban, and because a carelessly built dashboard is also the surface that teaches or defaults salons into using dark patterns against their OWN customers (for example a pre-checked paid visibility upsell, or an unguarded review-request tool, see finding on incentivized reviews).
findings.why: A law that binds only the surface with more scrutiny (customer-facing, investor-visible) and silently exempts the surface with less scrutiny (a B2B dashboard used by roughly 28 salons today, per _backend-system/research/security.md's own population estimate) creates exactly the blind spot dark-pattern research warns about: manipulative patterns migrate to wherever enforcement is weakest. Solen's own commission model (platform_fee via Stripe application_fee) gives it a direct financial incentive to nudge salons toward paid upsells, the same incentive-conflict PSYCHOLOGY.md's ethics lines exist to constrain on the customer side, with nothing said about the business side.
findings.local_evidence: PSYCHOLOGY.md line 7 (How to use it): 'Before designing or changing any customer surface: scan the 15 laws...', explicit customer-surface scoping. PSYCHOLOGY.md line 92 (enforcement, judgment laws): 'checked by the loop-reviewer on every customer-facing UI diff', the enforcement mechanism itself is scoped to exclude the dashboard by name. app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:155 (platform_fee via application_fee_amount) confirms Solen already takes a commission cut, i.e. has a live financial interest in salon-side upsell behavior.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i "dashboard|salon.side|business surface|owner surface" _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md -> zero hits; the word 'dashboard' does not appear anywhere in the 101-line file.
findings.existing_coverage: none: no PSYCHOLOGY.md law, hard line, or enforcement gate currently applies to app/[locale]/dashboard/* or components-legacy/dashboard/* by name or by scope.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md (add an explicit scope-extension line stating the hard lines bind app/[locale]/dashboard/* too) and the loop-reviewer's judgment-lens instructions
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule plus judgment law: extend the loop-reviewer's 'customer-facing UI diff' trigger to also fire on dashboard diffs; the machine gate (pre-edit-psychology-gate.py) is already scoped broadly to 'app/components tsx' per PSYCHOLOGY.md's own description and likely already fires on dashboard files for laws 6/9, so the gap is specifically the judgment-law half, not the machine half

findings.title: Marketing-notification cadence law states a UX cap, not the Swiss legal opt-in floor beneath it
findings.principle: Any automated mass marketing communication (SMS, push, email) to a Swiss consumer requires the recipient's prior, verifiable opt-in before the first send, per UWG Art. 3 Abs. 1 lit. o; sending on an opt-out-by-default basis is an unfair-competition offense carrying up to three years imprisonment or a fine under UWG Art. 23, not merely a retention-metric risk. Solen's marketing-category defaults must be documented as satisfying this opt-in requirement by design (default OFF, per PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14), and any future proposal to flip a marketing category on-by-default must be flagged as a legal question first, never shipped as a normal growth A/B test.
findings.why: PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14 frames the entire notification-cadence question as a retention and opt-out-rate problem ('volume, not content, drives opt-outs, 46% opt out at 2-5/week'). That framing invites a purely growth-metrics argument for turning a category on by default if the measured opt-out rate looks tolerable, when in Switzerland doing so for non-transactional marketing sends without prior consent is a criminal unfair-competition offense regardless of the resulting opt-out percentage. The current default-off setting happens to comply, but the file gives no reason a future engineer or growth push could not treat it as a soft UX preference and override it.
findings.local_evidence: PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14 (lines 54-55): 'Non-transactional pushes cap at 2-3/week; settings split by category (Buchungen ON, Angebote/Inspo OFF by default). Volume, not content, drives opt-outs (46% opt out at 2-5/week).' No UWG, opt-in, or consent-law citation anywhere in the file or in PSYCH_RETENTION.md's notification section (lines 33, 99, 206-207), which sources the same default-off recommendation purely from Baymard/Airship opt-out-rate data, never from Swiss law. WebSearch confirmed UWG Art. 3(1)(o) requires prior, documented opt-in for automated mass marketing via telecom channels, with criminal exposure under Art. 23 UWG.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i "UWG|opt-in|Einwilligung|unfair competition|consent.*marketing" _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md _backend-system -> zero hits tying notification defaults to Swiss consent law; the only 'consent' hits found relate to the cookie-consent banner (dp-pre-selection-is-not-consent in IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS_2026-07-16.md), a different surface.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the current default (marketing off, transactional on) already matches what UWG Art. 3(1)(o) requires, and the same 2026-07-07 audit already separately found the underlying enforcement is broken in code (see the consent silent-no-op finding). What's missing here is the law naming the legal floor at all, so a correct-by-accident default is not accidentally reversed later.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14 (add one sentence naming UWG Art. 3(1)(o) as the hard floor beneath the retention framing) and _rules/ (compliance note)
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule / checklist item: any PR changing a marketing-category default from OFF to ON must be flagged for compliance review, not shipped as a normal A/B test

findings.title: Brignull's dark-pattern taxonomy is named as vocabulary only; several categories have no binding Solen rule
findings.principle: Every one of the 14 named categories in the taxonomy Solen already cites (sneaking, nagging, obstruction, forced action, confirmshaming, comparison prevention, disguised ads, fake scarcity, fake social proof, fake urgency, hidden costs, hidden subscription, preselection, trick wording, visual interference) must resolve to an explicit PSYCHOLOGY.md hard line, a named DONT_ADD verdict, or a stated 'not yet applicable, revisit when X ships' note. A taxonomy that exists only so reviews can cite refusals by their industry names is decorative wherever a category was never individually checked against the actual product.
findings.why: A named taxonomy creates the appearance of complete ethical coverage without the substance: a reviewer citing the taxonomy can wrongly assume every category has been ruled on, when RATIONALE.md's own text says the section exists only for naming, not verdicts. Nagging (repeated permission or upsell re-asks), comparison prevention (inconsistent units or bundling that blocks price comparison), disguised ads (a future sponsored ranking rendered as organic, see the dedicated finding), hidden subscription (a future membership auto-renewal, already floated in PSYCH_RETENTION.md's contested section), and trick wording (double-negative settings copy) are all plausible Solen features with zero current ruling, unlike preselection, fake-scarcity, fake-social-proof, and confirmshaming, which do have explicit PSYCHOLOGY.md hard lines or a documented ALREADY_EXISTS verdict.
findings.local_evidence: RATIONALE.md line 815 (domain 23): 'This section exists so reviews can cite refusals by their industry names', explicitly naming vocabulary-only intent. Cross-checked against PSYCHOLOGY.md's 7 hard lines (lines 64-70): sneaking/hidden-costs (line 66), preselection (line 65), fake-scarcity/fake-social-proof/fake-urgency (lines 64, 69), confirmshaming (law 10, line 43) each have a named line. Nagging, comparison prevention, disguised ads, hidden subscription, and trick wording have zero corresponding PSYCHOLOGY.md line or IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS_2026-07-16.md verdict.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i "nagging|comparison prevention|disguised ad|hidden subscription|trick wording|visual interference" _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md -> zero hits (only the one RATIONALE.md naming line exists). grep -n "^### dm-|^### dp-" _design-system/research/IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS_2026-07-16.md -> 217 entries, none titled for these categories specifically; that file's dm-/dp- entries are IG-harvested visual and motion principles, not a re-run of Brignull's own list.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: 8-9 of 14 Brignull categories already have a Solen-specific ruling via PSYCHOLOGY.md hard lines or the 2026-07-16 verdict pass; the gap is the remaining 5-6, which the naming section's own text admits were never individually adjudicated.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/RATIONALE.md domain 23 (expand the naming list into a table with a verdict column) or a new _design-system/DARK_PATTERNS.md mirroring the IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS.md format
findings.enforcement: checklist plus judgment law: not machine-checkable, but the loop-reviewer's psychology lens (PSYCHOLOGY.md line 92) could add 'does this diff introduce nagging, comparison-blocking, disguised-ad, or trick-wording behavior' as an explicit bullet, since it currently lists only the 6 judgment laws from the 15, not the taxonomy categories

findings.title: Cancellation/exit-parity is a one-time verified audit finding, not a standing law or gate
findings.principle: Every flow that lets a user commit to something (booking, notification opt-in, a future membership) must let the user reverse it in no more taps and no more friction than the commit itself required, and this must be checked on every new commit-capable flow at ship time, not established once and assumed to hold forever. Any new feature, including a future pause-or-cancel membership flow already flagged as a live possibility in PSYCH_RETENTION.md's own contested section, must pass an explicit exit-parity check before ship, the same way it already passes a psychology-law check.
findings.why: The 2026-07-16 verdict on exit parity confirms Solen currently does the right thing (a 2-tap cancel versus a 4-step booking wizard), but the verdict itself states: 'No dedicated numbered law names step-parity explicitly', the finding is inferred from unrelated laws and confirmed by a hand-read of 4 files on one date. The machine gate (pre-edit-psychology-gate.py) only regexes for law 6 (rating without count) and law 9 (a hardcoded count literal); it cannot and does not check tap-count parity. A future membership flow could add a multi-step, retention-heavy cancel path with nothing catching it, because the only proof this does not happen today is a single dated manual read, not a rule.
findings.local_evidence: IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS_2026-07-16.md, dm-roach-motel-exit-parity section: 'No dedicated numbered law names step-parity explicitly.' PSYCHOLOGY.md line 91 (enforcement section): the only machine-gate scope named is law 6 and law 9; no step-count or tap-count check appears anywhere in the enforcement section (lines 87-94).
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i "exit parity|as easy to cancel|cancel.*symmetr|roach motel" _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md -> zero hits; the term and the check exist only in the one-time IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS_2026-07-16.md audit pass, not in the standing law file.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the current state passes (verified 2026-07-16), and RATIONALE.md's taxonomy-naming section (line 815) names 'obstruction (roach motel)' as a term; neither promotes it to a PSYCHOLOGY.md hard line or a loop-reviewer judgment-lens bullet, the actual enforcement mechanism this system relies on for everything else.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md hard lines (add: no commit-capable flow may require more steps to exit, cancel, or unsubscribe than it took to commit) and the loop-reviewer's judgment-law bullet list (PSYCHOLOGY.md line 92)
findings.enforcement: judgment law: add as an explicit loop-reviewer lens bullet, checked on every new commit or cancel flow diff, same tier as the existing 6 judgment laws

findings.title: No policy exists for incentivized, gated, or solicited-only-from-happy-customers reviews
findings.principle: A salon or Solen itself may never offer a discount, free service, credit, or any other consideration in exchange for a review, and may never selectively solicit reviews only from customers predicted to be satisfied (review-gating). Any review-request flow, salon-facing or customer-facing, must solicit all eligible customers uniformly regardless of predicted sentiment, and must never mention a reward tied to leaving a review, consistent with UCPD Annex I item 23(b)'s ban on misrepresenting reviews as genuine and consumer-originated without a disclosed connection.
findings.why: PSYCH_BUSINESS_IMPACT.md's own recommended lever is to make requesting a review from a salon's first bookings a tracked onboarding milestone, exactly the kind of feature that, built without a stated policy, drifts toward a salon-dashboard nudge like 'offer 10% off their next visit to boost your rating', a real and common salon-industry practice this research itself surfaces from vendor tools elsewhere. Every other trust-integrity question in Solen's system (fabricated counts, fake urgency, fake social proof) has a named hard line; review authenticity, the one input the entire 5-star rating system depends on, does not.
findings.local_evidence: PSYCH_BUSINESS_IMPACT.md line 19 explicitly recommends salons treat review-requesting as a tracked growth milestone, with no accompanying guardrail on how the request is made or whether it can be incentivized. No dashboard feature currently exists for this (grep for review-credit or review-reward code returns nothing), so this is a preventive gap, not a live violation.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i "incentiv.*review|review.*incentiv|review.*discount|discount.*review|review.*credit|credit.*review|review.*reward" _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md _backend-system app lib -> zero hits anywhere in the estate or the codebase.
findings.existing_coverage: none: PSYCHOLOGY.md law 6 covers how reviews are DISPLAYED (never bare, weighted by count) and hard line 1 covers fabricated review counts, but neither addresses how a review is SOLICITED or whether it can be incentivized, a distinct point in the pipeline with no coverage at all.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md (new hard line, adjacent to law 6) and any future salon-dashboard review-request feature spec
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule now, no live feature to gate; becomes a checklist item the moment any salon-facing review-request or review-reward feature is scoped

findings.title: Loyalty tier downgrade has a pre-drop nudge and a post-tier-up celebration, but no honest at-the-moment-of-loss disclosure
findings.principle: The moment a user's tier actually soft-drops (Platinum to Gold, or Gold to Base), the product must show a clear, named accounting of what changed: the new tier, the specific perks now locked (reusing the same unlocked-versus-locked rows already speced for the /rewards screen), and the concrete path back, delivered with the same design attention PSYCHOLOGY.md law 1 already mandates for the confirmation screen's peak-end moment, not silently reflected only as a changed badge the next time the app happens to open.
findings.why: LOYALTY_STRUCTURE.md specs an expiry nudge before the drop and a celebration on tier-up (SuccessMark plus haptic plus push plus email, explicitly stating 'treat tier-up as a product event, not a DB state change'), naming the asymmetry as a deliberate design decision for the positive case only. Nothing in the same document, or in PSYCHOLOGY.md's loss-framing law 10, specifies equivalent treatment for the downgrade EVENT itself, only the warning before it. A user who misses the window and drops silently learns about it by noticing a badge changed, which contradicts peak-end law 1's own logic (endings carry disproportionate memory weight) applied only to positive endings.
findings.local_evidence: LOYALTY_STRUCTURE.md section 7 (CRM surface, NON-NEGOTIABLE): 'Tier-up celebration: SuccessMark + haptic + push + email... Expiry nudge: your Gold status expires in 30 days.' No equivalent tier-down disclosure requirement anywhere in the same non-negotiable list or in section 2's soft-drop mechanic description (line 20).
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i "tier.down.*notif|downgrade.*disclos|drop.*celebrat|soft-drop.*notif" _design-system/LOYALTY_STRUCTURE.md _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md -> zero hits describing a post-drop disclosure moment; only the pre-drop expiry nudge and the tier-up celebration are specified.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: PSYCHOLOGY.md hard line 4 requires grace before any tier drop (satisfied by the soft-drop-one-tier mechanic) and law 10 requires honest, non-fabricated loss-framing copy; neither specifies what happens at the actual moment the drop occurs, only what must happen before it.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOYALTY_STRUCTURE.md section 7 (CRM surface) and a cross-reference from PSYCHOLOGY.md law 1 or law 10
findings.enforcement: checklist item for the /rewards and loyalty-notification build, since LOYALTY_STRUCTURE.md is a build contract not yet fully shipped per its own section 8 pre-launch calibration note

findings.title: Personalization law requires additive ranking but names no user-facing visibility or opt-out control
findings.principle: Wherever a ranking or feed is influenced by inferred personal signals (booking history, saved favorites, Inspo DNA points), the user must be able to see that personalization is active and switch to a neutral, unranked view on request, even though the underlying signal never hides inventory (law 15's existing requirement). Additive-not-filtering avoids one harm (hidden options); it does not by itself give the user visibility into, or control over, being profiled, which is a separate expectation for any automated personal-data-driven ranking.
findings.why: Law 15 solves the 'do not hide the catalog' problem but answers a different question than 'does the user know, and can they turn it off.' A user who never sees any indication that Inspo or search-adjacent ranking is personalized has no way to exercise even an informal preference, let alone the transparency users increasingly expect for behavioral profiling, the same instinct behind Solen's own default-off marketing category in law 14. Since the underlying service_categories personalization backend is explicitly dormant, this is the correct moment to decide the control exists before reactivation, not retrofit it after users notice unexplained ranking changes.
findings.local_evidence: PSYCHOLOGY.md law 15 (lines 57-58): 'Boost and label ("Für dich"), keep the full catalog reachable... Applies to the dormant service_categories personalization backend and the Inspo feed ranking.' No mention of a user-facing toggle, disclosure, or 'why am I seeing this' affordance anywhere in the law text.

findings.existing_coverage: partial: law 15's additive requirement already prevents the worst-case harm of hidden inventory; the appendix note in PSYCH_PSYCHOLOGY.md line 121 (add a because-you-saved-X reason line) gestures at transparency but was never promoted into the 15 laws or a hard line, so it carries no enforcement weight.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md law 15 (extend with a visibility/opt-out sentence) before service_categories personalization reactivates
findings.enforcement: checklist item gating personalization-backend reactivation, since the feature is dormant, not live

findings.title: Disguised-ads and sponsored-ranking have zero ruling, a preventive gap ahead of any monetized-visibility feature
findings.principle: If Solen ever ships a paid visibility, boosted-listing, or promoted-ranking feature for salons, any promoted result must carry a persistent, unambiguous 'Gesponsert'/'Sponsored' label at the same visual weight as the salon name, must never be visually indistinguishable from organic ranking, and must never let a paid boost override a real safety or quality signal (a poorly-rated salon must never outrank a well-rated one purely by payment), consistent with UCPD Annex I's ban on disguised advertising and the same first-principles reasoning Solen already applied to reject Solen-side decoy pricing.
findings.why: Solen's own commission-based business model creates the same incentive structure that leads marketplaces toward pay-to-rank features once monetization pressure increases; the product has already reasoned through and refused a structurally similar temptation once (decoy pricing, DONT_ADD verdict citing 'Solen unilaterally distorting a salon's real catalog'), but that reasoning was never generalized into a standing rule for the more common and more likely future monetization lever, paid ranking or visibility.
findings.local_evidence: grep for sponsored, promoted, or paid-boost ranking code in app/ and lib/ returns zero hits: no such feature exists today, confirming this is purely preventive. IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS_2026-07-16.md's dp-decoy-effect verdict (line 355) is the closest existing reasoning in the estate, applied to a different monetization idea, not to sponsored ranking itself.
